gaps.explanation: Proprietary statement p6 (Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds) prints Electric Fund, Water Fund, Sewer Fund and Nonmajor Landfill Fund columns (plus Total and Internal Service Fund, not used); no business-type line is in detail[] and the trim has no utility schedule. JSON receipts = total operating revenues + interest income + intergovernmental/grants + gain on disposal + special assessments (134,063,088), so the same rows are added per fund. Operating revenues: Electric 105,280,550 (64,198,552 + 2,048,447 + 37,256,291 + 1,777,260), Water 6,925,897 (6,595,172 + 218,384 + 504 + 111,837), Sewer 15,129,374 (14,978,047 + 23,594 + 127,733), Landfill 3,446,805 (3,439,019 + 7,786) = 130,782,626; Interest income 196,884 + 23,550 + 62,164 + 163,608 = 446,206; Intergovernmental/grants (Sewer) 1,981,355; Gain on disposal of assets (Electric) 12,817; Special assessments (Sewer) 840,084. Sum 134,063,088 = gap.

The 13,691 the gap file counts as schedule debt proceeds is the p9 'Proceeds from sales of capital assets' line (detail index of the General Fund budgetary schedule, other financing), which is a sale of capital assets, not debt; after the add, real debt-proceeds detail = 431,241 = statement. Not added: the p4 General Fund 'Proceeds from sales of capital asset' 64,080 (GAAP) - the same row is already in detail on the budgetary basis as 13,691 (p9), so adding it would double count (different basis).
